cards.name: SCATCH
cards.summary: Grayscale brush image shipped in CorelDRAW's Custom Data/Brushes folder (128x128 px BMP). The thumbnail is the file itself (file image, not a script render): a tangle of thin, straight white scratch strokes running diagonally (lower left to upper right) over a soft round white glow, on black. The name reads like a misspelt 'scratch'; the picture is a scratched-glow burst, not the single line of the 'scratch' file.
avoid: A clean single line: use 'scratch' or 'STDLINE' instead.
Expecting a CorelDRAW (Draw) preset list entry: no Draw menu or property bar loads this file; import it as a bitmap.
Colour work: it is 8-bit grayscale; tint it (Bitmaps > Mode) or use it as a transparency / mask source.
cards.applies_to: bitmap: a loose 8-bit grayscale BMP brush image (white = paint / opaque, black = none, as brush nibs and masks read it), not a live effect on a selected object
cards.how_to_apply: No CorelDRAW menu, docker or property-bar list applies it, and the harvest records only the file: C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Brushes\SCATCH.BMP. Use it as a bitmap: File > Import (Ctrl+I), or script ActiveLayer.Import("C:\Program Files\Corel\CorelDRAW Graphics Suite\25\Custom Data\Brushes\SCATCH.BMP"), then use it as a stamp, mask or transparency source. In Corel PHOTO-PAINT it can serve as a custom brush-nib image (Brush settings, custom nib; route not tested by the harvest).

verified.note: A tangle of thin straight white scratch strokes running lower left to upper right over a soft round white glow, on black.

review.changes: avoid: 'Bitmap > Mode' corrected to 'Bitmaps > Mode', the harvested menu path (cdr_menu.json Bitmaps/Mode)
